title: B2+ · L45 — Startup vocabulary
description: Jerga startup: pivot, runway, MVP, churn, product-market fit, y ecosystem language.

questions.prompt: En un board meeting el CFO habla de la supervivencia.
questions.question: 'Runway' in startup terms means:
options: How many months of cash the company has before running out.
The time from idea to launch.
questions.explanation: Runway = tiempo (meses) antes de bancarrota si no llegan revenue nuevo o funding. Metafora de aviacion: cuanta pista tienes antes de despegar o estrellarte. Metrica de supervivencia startup #1. '12+ months of runway' es healthy; '<6 months' es zona roja; '<3 months' es crisis. Registro: startup / VC / founder. Formula: runway = cash actual / (burn rate mensual). 'Extend runway' = alargar pista via reducir burn o subir revenue. 'Hit the runway' = quedarte sin cash. Error hispano: pronunciar como en espanol — es /ˈrʌnweɪ/ con acento en 'RUN'.
examples: We've got 18 months of runway after the seed round — plenty of time to hit PMF. → founder confident
Cutting burn extends runway — the fastest lever we have right now. → decision defensiva

questions.prompt: En un pitch un fundador explica su enfoque de producto.
questions.question: 'MVP' stands for:
questions.explanation: MVP = Minimum Viable Product. La version mas pequena posible que valide la hipotesis central del producto con usuarios reales. Concepto del Lean Startup (Eric Ries, 2011). Ubicuo en startup vocabulary. Idea clave: NO es un producto pobre — es un producto MINIMO pero VIABLE (usable y valioso para early adopters). Registro: startup / product. CUIDADO con el uso mal aplicado: 'MVP' se ha convertido en excusa para shippear productos rotos. La regla original: 'if you're not embarrassed by your MVP, you shipped too late' — pero embarrassed no significa broken. Error hispano cultural: sobre-engineer el MVP por pursuit de perfeccion; el punto es aprender rapido.
examples: We shipped the MVP in six weeks — ugly but functional. Learned a ton. → practica lean
MVP first, polish later — that's the mantra, but you still need it to actually work. → matiz importante

questions.statement: 'Pivot' means changing the startup's direction significantly based on what you've learned from customers or data.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. Pivot = cambio significativo de estrategia (producto, segmento, business model) MANTENIENDO el aprendizaje acumulado. Termino de Eric Ries (Lean Startup). Pivots legendarios: Slack empezo como juego (Glitch); Instagram empezo como check-in app (Burbn); YouTube empezo como sitio de dating; Twitter empezo como plataforma de podcasts (Odeo). Registro: startup / VC. Tipos de pivot: customer segment pivot, problem pivot, technology pivot, business model pivot, revenue model pivot. NO es lo mismo que 'give up' — es reorientar CON informacion. Error hispano: usar 'pivot' como sinonimo de 'cambio' generico — en startup context es cambio ESTRATEGICO basado en learning.
examples: We pivoted from B2C to B2B after six months of user feedback showed enterprise had the real budget. → pivot de segmento
Great startups pivot at least once — the trick is knowing when and how sharply. → observacion VC

questions.prompt: En una board de SaaS company se destaca la metrica mas dolorosa.
questions.question: 'Churn' refers to:
options: The process of making butter industrially.
The rate at which existing customers stop using the product / cancel.
The rate of new customer signups.
questions.explanation: Churn = tasa de cancelacion. Cliente adquirido → se va = churn. Enemy #1 de las metricas SaaS. Con churn alto, el growth es ilusion: adquieres 100, pierdes 90, crecimiento neto = 10, y ademas has gastado CAC (customer acquisition cost) en los 90 que se fueron. Registro: SaaS / product. Tipos: 'customer churn' (# de clientes que se van), 'revenue churn' (perdida en $), 'gross churn' vs 'net churn' (net incluye upsells/expansion que compensan). Benchmarks: SaaS B2C ~5%/mes es normal; SaaS enterprise <1%/mes es healthy. Error hispano: la palabra no tiene equivalente elegante en espanol — 'tasa de baja' o 'tasa de fuga' se usan pero el termino ingles domina.
examples: Monthly churn is at 5% — too high for enterprise, marginal for B2C. → benchmark
Reducing churn beats increasing acquisition — leaky bucket problem. → mantra SaaS

questions.text: We hit product-market fit around month eighteen when retention curves finally started to plateau instead of dropping to zero.
questions.explanation: Discurso founder maduro. 'Product-market fit' (PMF), 'retention curves', 'plateau instead of dropping to zero' — signal empirico de PMF: las curvas de retencion se aplanan en vez de caer a 0%. Feature de connected speech: 'hit product-market' /hɪt ˈprɒdʌkt ˈmɑːrkət/ — la /t/ final de 'hit' se pega a la /p/; 'plateau' /plæˈtoʊ/ o /ˈplætoʊ/ — pronunciacion francesa mantenida. 'Instead of' /ɪnˈsted əv/ con weak form del 'of'. Registro: founder / VC diligence conversation. Concepto del PMF de Sean Ellis, Andrew Chen y Marc Andreessen: 'the only thing that matters'.
examples: PMF is when users would be very disappointed without your product — Sean Ellis's test. → definicion operativa
Retention curves that flatten out are the strongest empirical signal of PMF. → dato clave

questions.prompt: El CFO de una startup explica la metrica financiera clave.
questions.question: 'Burn rate' is:
options: The risk of fire in the office.
Monthly cash spent minus revenue — the net cash outflow.
questions.explanation: Burn rate = cash consumido por mes NETO de revenue. Determina el runway (runway = cash / burn). 'Gross burn' = total gastado; 'net burn' = gastado - revenue (mas comun cuando la gente dice 'burn'). Registro: startup finance / VC. Familia: 'default alive' (revenue crece > costes, no necesitas raise) vs 'default dead' (necesitas raise para sobrevivir — Paul Graham). 'Zero burn' o 'profitable' es el santo grial. Error hispano: 'burn rate' no tiene traduccion elegante — 'tasa de quema' se usa pero suena raro; el termino ingles domina en la industria hispana startup.
examples: Our net burn is 400K per month against 200K in revenue — gross burn is 600K. → transparencia CFO
Cutting burn is the fastest way to survive tough markets when raising is hard. → estrategia defensiva

questions.prompt: Empareja cada termino de ecosystem startup con su definicion:

pairs.right: Meses de dinero antes de quebrar

questions.explanation: Vocabulario esencial del startup ecosystem global. 'Traction' es evidencia empirica de adopcion — MRR growing, retention curves, waitlist size, user testimonials; 'story without traction' es solo pitch. 'Unicorn' (termino de Aileen Lee, 2013) era raro; ahora hay ~1,200 unicornios globales, y termino 'decacorn' (>$10B) y 'hectocorn' (>$100B) para los mega-raros. Registro: VC / startup / tech journalism. Error hispano: 'traction' se usa en spanish oral tambien; los founders hispanos que trabajan con VCs anglo lo usan sin traducir.
examples: We're gaining traction with early adopters — 300 paying customers in three months. → dato concreto
Only about one in a thousand startups reaches unicorn status — most fail or exit smaller. → realidad estadistica

questions.target: We raised a Series A on the back of strong retention and 10% monthly growth — investors want to see PMF and momentum.
questions.explanation: Discurso fundraising senior tipico. 'Raised a Series A' (cerrar ronda A), 'on the back of' (respaldados por), 'strong retention' (metrica clave), '10% monthly growth' (dato concreto), 'PMF and momentum' (los dos senales que VCs buscan). Ritmo natural: pausa breve tras 'growth,', enfasis tonico en 'strong', '10%', y 'momentum'; tono descendente y firme al cierre. Contracciones no aplican en registro semi-formal de founder pitch. Registro: founder / fundraising. Estructura clasica de founder narrative: milestone + evidencia + tesis del mercado.
examples: We closed our seed and are heads-down on PMF for the next twelve months. → founder focus
Bridge round to extend runway while we hit our metrics before the A. → tactica de financiacion

questions.prompt: En un pitch un fundador presume su modelo autosuficiente.
questions.question: 'Bootstrapping' means:
options: Growing the company without external funding — self-funded via revenue.
questions.explanation: Bootstrapping = crecer con revenue propio, sin VC (o con capital minimo de founders). Trade-off: mas independencia y equity retenido, pero crecimiento mas lento. Bootstrapped famosos: Basecamp, Mailchimp (vendido a Intuit por $12B en 2021 — bootstrap no impide exits enormes), Zoho, Braintree (parcial). Registro: startup. Familia: 'self-funded' (equivalente), 'ramen profitable' (Paul Graham — ganas lo justo para vivir sin sueldo VC-inflado). Origen: idiom 'pull yourself up by your bootstraps' (levantarte por tus propios medios). Error hispano: escribir 'boot strapping' separado — es 'bootstrapping' junto, siempre.
examples: We bootstrapped for the first three years — no external capital, growth funded by customers. → historia clasica
Bootstrapping preserves equity but slows scaling — trade-off you have to live with. → matiz honesto

questions.statement: 'Cap table' shows the ownership structure of a company's equity — who owns what percentage.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. Cap table (capitalization table) = tabla que muestra la composicion accionaria: founders, employees (via options/ESOP), y investors (por ronda y por clase de acciones). Crucial en fundraising y en M&A — un cap table 'sucio' (demasiados inversores pequenos, terminos raros de rondas anteriores, options mal gestionadas) puede matar rondas futuras o exits. Registro: startup finance / legal. Herramientas populares: Carta, Pulley, LTSE Equity. Familia: 'dilution' (perdida de % ownership al emitir nuevas acciones), 'pre-money' vs 'post-money valuation', 'liquidation preference'. Error hispano frecuente: dejar la gestion del cap table para 'despues' — los errores tempranos son muy caros de deshacer.
examples: Founders got diluted from 60% to 40% after Series B — normal for that stage. → dinamica standard
A clean cap table matters more than founders realize for later rounds and exits. → advice VC

questions.prompt: Se cierra una ronda A y hay que revisar el papel principal.
questions.question: 'Term sheet' is:
options: A non-binding document outlining the key terms of an investment.
An employment contract for the CEO.
A marketing plan for the launch.
questions.explanation: Term sheet = documento pre-cierre que establece los terminos principales de la inversion (valoracion, size, class of shares, board seats, liquidation preference, anti-dilution, pro-rata, etc.). Non-binding generalmente (con excepciones como no-shop clauses y confidentiality). Setea expectations antes de meses de due diligence y legal work. Registro: startup / VC / legal. LEER CADA CLAUSULA con abogado experimentado en venture — algunas clauses parecen inocuas y son devastadoras (participating preferred, full-ratchet anti-dilution). Familia: 'lead investor' (quien setea los terms), 'follow-on' (inversores que aceptan los terms), 'convertible note', 'SAFE' (Simple Agreement for Future Equity).
examples: We signed the term sheet last week — closing in about 30 days pending diligence. → timeline tipico
Read every clause of the term sheet carefully with a specialized lawyer — cheap now, expensive later. → advice

questions.text: The founder-market fit was strong — she'd lived the pain point herself for years before starting the company.
questions.explanation: Discurso VC-perspective sofisticado. 'Founder-market fit' (concepto reciente que complementa a PMF: el founder tiene ventaja unica en ese mercado por experiencia previa), 'lived the pain point herself' — indicator que VCs valoran cada vez mas. Feature de connected speech: 'she'd lived' /ʃiːd lɪvd/ — la /d/ del 'had' contraido se pega a la /l/; 'pain point herself' /peɪn pɔɪnt hərˈself/ con enlazado suave. Registro: VC diligence conversation. Familia: 'insight', 'unfair advantage' (ventaja competitiva estructural), 'domain expertise'. Idea clave: los mejores fundadores han sufrido el problema que resuelven.
examples: The best founders have lived the problem — they don't need market research to understand pain. → axioma VC
Founder-market fit predicts success as much as, and sometimes more than, product-market fit. → observacion moderna

questions.prompt: Un VC explica el objetivo financiero final.
questions.question: 'Exit' in startup terms means:
options: Selling the company (acquisition) or going public (IPO) — a liquidity event.
questions.explanation: Exit = liquidity event que permite a founders e inversores monetizar su equity. Dos tipos principales: (1) acquisition/M&A — otra empresa compra; (2) IPO — cotizar en bolsa. Menos comunes: secondary (vender shares privadas a otro investor), SPAC merger (via companies vacias). 'Successful exit' es el goal financiero de VCs y suele ser el goal financiero de founders. Registro: VC / startup / financial. Realidad estadistica dura: la mayoria de startups NO tienen exit — simplemente fracasan (~70% de startups VC-backed). De las que exitan, la distribucion es power-law: pocos exits enormes generan la mayor parte del return del portfolio de un VC.
examples: The exit was two billion in cash and stock — one of the biggest of the year. → dato ejecutivo
Most startups don't have an exit — they just fail or stagnate. That's the reality. → matiz honesto

questions.statement: 'Founder-led sales' means the founder personally sells the product to early customers.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. Founder-led sales = el founder(a) cierra deals iniciales personalmente, especialmente en enterprise/B2B. Critical para early stage: (1) el founder oye objections en crudo; (2) ajusta producto rapido; (3) VCs valoran el customer development directo; (4) senal de conviction. Standard practice hasta al menos $2-5M ARR, dependiendo del segment. Registro: startup / sales. Error clasico: hire un VP of Sales demasiado pronto — antes de que el playbook este validado, el VP no puede escalar lo que aun no funciona. Familia: 'founder-led growth', 'do things that don't scale' (Paul Graham essay).
examples: You need founder-led sales until at least $10M ARR in enterprise — the CEO is the best salesperson. → regla
Hiring a VP of Sales too early is a classic mistake — they inherit a playbook that doesn't exist yet. → advertencia

questions.target: We're heads-down on getting to PMF — once we see the retention curves flatten, we'll open a Series A round to scale.
questions.explanation: Discurso founder autentico y VC-savvy. 'Heads-down' (colocacion — enfocados sin distracciones), 'getting to PMF' (proceso, no evento), 'retention curves flatten' (signal empirico), 'open a Series A round to scale' (siguiente milestone). Ritmo natural: pausa breve tras 'PMF —', enfasis tonico en 'flatten' y 'scale'. Contracciones obligatorias: 'we're', 'we'll'. Registro: founder pitch / update to advisors. Estructura clasica: focus actual + trigger que abre el siguiente stage + plan de siguiente stage. Cadencia de founder que ha estudiado la playbook.
examples: Focused on burn and PMF — fundraising is a distraction until we get there. → disciplina founder
MVP shipped; now testing willingness to pay before we even think about raising. → sequencia disciplinada
